what: Short-sequence Core ML graph for the cross-encoder reranker (coreml_rerank.py)
machine: Apple M1 Pro, macOS 15, coremltools 9.0, ComputeUnit.ALL
note_on_the_knee: 128 is a knee, not a linear trend: 192 is 1.7x slower than 128 and 256 is 3.9x slower, so SEQ_FAST=128 is chosen on the measurement, not by halving.

real_pair_token_lengths.conclusion: real (query, passage) pairs sit far under 128, so the short graph carries the overwhelming majority of pairs

faithfulness_vs_512_graph.the_one_full_order_difference: ranks 6 and 7 of the tail swapped between two passages whose 512 scores were BIT-IDENTICAL (-11.44531, gap exactly 0.0) - a tie-break, not a semantic disagreement

end_to_end_rerank_K20.note: end-to-end is lower than the 9.70x per-predict figure because it includes tokenization and the Python per-pair loop

safety.routing_rule: a pair uses the short graph ONLY when its tokenized length is already <= SEQ_FAST, so routing can never truncate anything the 512 graph would have kept
safety.optional: the short graph is optional at every step - an older cache without it, or one where it fails to convert or validate, runs every pair at SEQ exactly as before

upgrade_cost_measured_against_the_real_d.how: copied the live ~/Library/Application Support/DARWIN cache (which had only rerank_b1.mlpackage + tokenizer) and called ensure_loaded() on it
upgrade_cost_measured_against_the_real_d.what_that_covers: loading the HF checkpoint + converting BOTH graphs + validate-load + atomic publish. An earlier note in this branch disclosed ~11.5 s, which was the CONVERSION step alone and understated what a deployed machine actually pays.
upgrade_cost_measured_against_the_real_d.when_it_is_paid: at server startup via server.preload (the eager warm), not inside a request
upgrade_cost_measured_against_the_real_d.result: both graphs present afterwards, fast graph loaded, reranking still correct

ane_utilization.note: Same check for the reranker: identical placement between the two graphs.
